column1: # id|pattern|playstyle|teamfight decision|strengths|weakness and response

Aatrox|bruiser|Control the edge of each Q swing, then move between casts. Use a short dash to correct the angle rather than spending every tool to close distance.|Approach beside your frontline. Use chains to restrict an escape and aim subsequent swings at the route out; activate World Ender before sustained contact.|Repeated area damage and healing reward accurate hits during extended fights.|Missed swings remove both pressure and recovery. If enemies spread or kite away, regroup instead of chasing outside ally reach.

Ahri|assassin|Use wave control and movement to create Charm angles. Trade with the returning orb while keeping a route back to safety.|Threaten a side angle, land Charm on a reachable target, then use Spirit Rush to adjust position. Keep a dash available until the enemy response is clear.|Pick potential and repeat movement let her punish exposed targets and change angles.|A missed Charm weakens the commitment. Do not spend all dashes chasing a carry through their team.

Akali|assassin|Alternate spell hits with movement out of the passive ring and empowered attacks. Treat shroud as time to reposition.|Enter after key enemy control is used. Use shroud to break targeting and choose whether the marked Shuriken Flip target is still safe to follow.|Multiple movement tools and burst threaten vulnerable backline targets.|Shroud does not make every source of damage harmless. Avoid following a marked target into a cluster with no exit.

Akshan|marksman|Combine attacks with Avengerang and use terrain to create swing paths. Roam only after accounting for the wave you leave.|Shoot a safe target first, then swing around an edge when collision paths are clear. A Scoundrel is valuable only if pursuing them will not lose the fight.|Mobile ranged pressure and Scoundrel takedowns can change the cost of a close fight.|Heroic Swing can end on collision. Check terrain and enemy bodies before relying on it as an escape.

Alistar|engage|Threaten a knock-up and displacement without using them on every opportunity. Stand where either a teammate or a target is in reach.|Choose between engaging with Headbutt into Pulverize and knocking a diver away from your carry. Use Unbreakable Will when enemy control and damage arrive.|Reliable close-range disruption and damage reduction give allies time to act.|A knockback in the wrong direction can rescue an enemy. Check follow-up distance before launching yourself forward.

Ambessa|bruiser|Weave attacks between abilities to recover energy and use the following dashes to stay at effective range.|Choose a Public Execution line with a landing point your team can reach. After arrival, alternate attacks and casts rather than emptying energy in one sequence.|Repeated movement, shielding and target access support sustained melee pressure.|Her ultimate selects the farthest champion in its line. A careless angle can strand her beyond the intended target.

Amumu|engage|Use Bandage Toss to reach opponents and apply pressure through repeated close contact. Keep allies close enough to benefit from your control.|Look for a clustered group with allied damage in range. Follow the bandage with the ultimate, then stay near targets while allies finish the fight.|Area crowd control can hold several enemies in place for allied spells.|Landing a bandage is not sufficient reason to engage. If your damage dealers cannot follow, hold it or use it defensively.

Anivia|control|Shape movement with the wall and storm, then use Frostbite after the correct chilling setup. Prepare space before opponents reach you.|Place the storm across an approach and use the wall to split the enemy formation. Keep the stun available for a diver if your team lacks protection.|Persistent area control and terrain creation punish narrow approaches.|Walls can also trap allies. Leave a friendly retreat route and do not assume the egg will survive without protection.

Annie|control|Track the passive stun and use its threat to control short-range exchanges. Keep enough resources for the full follow-up.|Prepare the stun before contact. Use Tibbers on an accessible cluster or hold a targeted stun to stop the enemy that can kill your carry.|Clear burst and dependable stun setup make follow-up easy for allies.|Short reach can force dangerous approaches. Use vision and allied setup rather than walking straight through enemy poke.

Aphelios|marksman|Plan around the two equipped weapons and their remaining ammunition. Different pairs change your reach, control and damage pattern.|Read the main-hand weapon before Moonlight Vigil. Use the pair you have: range for safe pressure, control to catch, or close-range damage only with protection.|Weapon combinations offer several ways to contribute to a fight.|The wrong weapon assumption can ruin a sequence. Check ammunition before contact and avoid forcing a close-range pattern into enemy control.

Ashe|marksman|Keep attacks flowing on reachable targets and use slows to maintain distance. Scout uncertain routes with Hawkshot.|Use the arrow when allies can act on the stun, or save it for a diver. Continue attacking the nearest safe target while moving away from threats.|Slows, scouting and long-range initiation provide value beyond damage.|She has no basic dash. Stay beside protection and avoid chasing a slowed enemy into an unseen flank.

AurelionSol|control|Collect Stardust through ability use while protecting the space needed to channel. Scale your plan around available area control.|Put Singularity on a route enemies need, then channel from protected ground. Use flight to reposition only after checking where hostile control can intercept it.|Growing area coverage and sustained breath damage reward controlled fights.|Channels and flight paths can expose him. Stop dealing damage and reposition when the enemy can reach the channel location.

Aurora|control|Create repeated spell and attack contacts to release spirits. Use her hops to change spacing rather than standing still for every exchange.|Cast Between Worlds across useful space, then use its edge travel to change angles. Draw curse returns through opponents while keeping a safe landing point.|Flexible movement and area pressure let her work around the edge of a fight.|The zone slows enemies; do not treat it as a guaranteed prison. Plan for enemies leaving and avoid hopping into waiting control.

Azir|marksman|Position soldiers where enemies need to stand and move yourself separately from them. Save a soldier route for retreat.|Default to sustained soldier attacks behind protection. Use Emperor's Divide to reject divers; commit to an offensive shuffle only with a clear allied follow-up.|Soldier reach supports sustained damage and control over a chosen zone.|Moving soldiers away can remove your safe damage zone. A flashy dash into five enemies can trade away your team's main damage source.

Bard|protect|Time roams around ally safety and collect chimes along useful routes. Look for Cosmic Binding lines that meet a second target or wall.|Use stasis to isolate part of a fight, then prepare the follow-up before it ends. Keep a portal escape in mind and remember enemies can use it too.|Terrain travel and stasis can change where and when a fight happens.|Stasis affects allies as well as enemies. Avoid freezing targets during an ally's committed burst.

Belveth|bruiser|Build attack speed through farming and takedowns, then alternate attacks with directional dashes. Plan around which dash directions remain.|Fight a reachable target until a safe coral opportunity appears. Use Royal Maelstrom to weather a damage window, not as a reason to stand inside all enemy control.|Extended attacks and transformation rewards can turn an initial takedown into momentum.|Coral can lure her into danger. Check surrounding enemies before consuming it, and do not assume the stationary channel is an escape.

Blitzcrank|engage|Use the threat of Rocket Grab to deny space. A held hook can pressure opponents more than a low-chance cast.|Pull a target your team can safely eliminate, then chain the knock-up and silence. Against a diving tank, use control defensively instead of delivering them to your carry.|A single pick can create a numbers advantage before the main fight.|Hooking the wrong enemy can start their ideal engage. Judge the target, not only the chance of hitting the skillshot.

Brand|control|Sequence different spells to build Blaze and arrange the stun with a prior burn. Look for enemies close enough to spread effects.|Fight near an ally who can screen divers. Apply spells across clustered enemies and choose an ultimate target with useful bounce paths.|Stacked burns and spreading damage threaten grouped teams.|No dash and conditional stun leave him exposed if spells miss. Keep a defensive stun sequence available against immediate threats.

Braum|protect|Stay close to the ally who needs protection and apply the first Concussive Blows stack for teammates to extend.|Face Unbreakable toward the relevant projectile source. Mark the diver and use the ultimate to disrupt the approach, then move with your carry.|Projectile interception and shared stun stacking strengthen coordinated defense.|The shield has a direction and does not solve every angle. Reposition if enemies attack from two sides.

Briar|bruiser|Plan the end of Blood Frenzy before starting it. Use controlled entry and keep Chilling Scream available to regain choice.|Confirm the destination of the ultimate before committing. Enter with allies, then use the scream to end a dangerous pursuit or push threats toward terrain.|Sustained pursuit and healing reward fights where targets cannot easily leave.|Frenzy can carry her into an unwanted target or tower. A ready cancel is part of the engage plan, not an optional extra.

Caitlyn|marksman|Use range to pressure safely and place traps where movement is constrained. Preserve the net for a threat that closes distance.|Set traps around the team's holding position before contact. Attack from behind the frontline and follow allied control with a trap where practical.|Long attack reach and prepared traps support siege and controlled objective setups.|Traps need useful placement and her escape can be pressured. Do not walk forward just to force a trapped-target follow-up through danger.

Camille|duelist|Prepare the second Precision Protocol hit and use terrain to set up Hookshot. Choose short trades with a planned exit.|Wait for allied damage to approach, then isolate a priority target with the ultimate. Use the initial leap deliberately to avoid a critical response.|Terrain access and target isolation can remove an enemy carry's movement options.|A trapped target can still fight and receive help. Do not isolate yourself with a stronger opponent beyond your team's reach.

Cassiopeia|control|Land poison before committing to repeated Twin Fangs. Keep moving between casts and reserve space behind you.|Use Miasma to obstruct an approach or escape, then damage the nearest safe poisoned target. Save the ultimate for enemies facing into your team when possible.|Sustained spell damage and grounding punish opponents who stay within her zone.|Missed poison reduces the payoff of continued casting. Avoid exhausting resources on a target you cannot hold in range.

Chogath|engage|Use the threat of Rupture to control approaches and layer silence after allies restrict movement. Build durable presence through Feast opportunities.|Stand between the enemy and your damage dealers. Use control on divers, and reserve Feast for a reachable finish or objective decision rather than chasing through the team.|Multiple forms of disruption and growing durability make him hard to ignore.|Delayed control can miss mobile targets. Follow allied setup or place it on a necessary route instead of always aiming at current position.

Corki|marksman|Combine ranged attacks with spell pressure and preserve Valkyrie when the enemy can engage. Use missiles to test space before committing.|Start with ranged damage, then attack targets you can reach without crossing the frontline. Use Valkyrie to reposition when a diver changes the safe angle.|Mixed spell and attack pressure lets him contribute before and during contact.|Using the dash for minor damage can remove his escape. Keep it for a real positional gain or a confirmed finish.

Darius|bruiser|Extend contact when the wave and enemy positions permit it. Place the outer edge of Decimate to secure the useful hit.|Build Hemorrhage on a reachable opponent rather than running through the frontline immediately. Use the ultimate when the target is within a realistic finishing window.|Stacking pressure and execution rewards make sustained close fights dangerous.|Kiting and interrupted contact can prevent his payoff. Use cover and allied control; stop chasing when the team can no longer follow.

Diana|bruiser|Use Moonlight to prepare a dash sequence and combine attacks with spells. Decide whether a second dash is for entry or adjustment.|Enter after allies are ready to damage the same group. Pull enemies with Moonfall, then remain near allied follow-up instead of diving alone for a large hit count.|Fast access and area burst punish grouped opponents.|A successful entry can still leave her surrounded. Count enemy escape and defensive tools before spending the approach.

Draven|marksman|Catch axes when the landing area is safe and keep pressure through attacks. Treat each catch as a movement decision.|Attack the nearest safe target while steering catches toward protected ground. Use Stand Aside to interrupt an approach rather than chasing every dropped axe.|Strong attack pressure rewards clean axe handling and sustained contact.|Axe locations advertise movement. Give up an axe that would put you in a hook, stun or unsafe forward position.

DrMundo|bruiser|Use cleavers to approach and keep pressure without committing every time. Recover and return rather than forcing low-health fights without a plan.|Absorb pressure on a useful route while allies deal damage. Time Maximum Dosage around expected damage and pursue only while your team retains position.|Durability, recovery and repeated slows let him occupy contested space.|Being durable does not give reliable hard control. If the carry is unreachable, obstruct the frontline instead of leaving your allies exposed.

Ekko|assassin|Use Timewinder and attacks to trigger short bursts, then move away. Set Parallel Convergence where the fight will be, not where it was.|Approach from an angle and threaten the delayed zone. Check the visible return location before committing; Chronobreak can recover position only if that location is useful.|Burst, delayed control and a return tool enable repeated attempts.|The return point can be watched or become unsafe. Do not treat the ultimate as an unconditional rescue from control.

Elise|assassin|Use human-form setup to find a Cocoon, then switch to spider form only when closing distance has a purpose.|Look for a catch on an isolated edge before the full fight. Hold Rappel to avoid a key response or change target access after the initial burst.|A ranged catch followed by melee pressure can remove an exposed target quickly.|Entering spider range without landing setup makes retreat harder. Against grouped teams, use picks and defensive Cocoon instead of frontally diving.

Evelynn|assassin|Approach through unseen space and plan around Allure's setup. Keep an exit angle before revealing yourself.|Wait until the enemy's attention is elsewhere, then threaten a vulnerable target. Use the ultimate's backward movement to leave the dangerous part of the fight.|Camouflage and burst create pressure on isolated enemies and side routes.|Detection and grouped protection restrict access. Do not force a flank that the enemy has already seen and prepared for.

Ezreal|marksman|Use Mystic Shot to maintain pressure while moving between safe firing angles. Weave attacks when the threat range allows it.|Keep Arcane Shift for the first dangerous engage unless a forward move is clearly safe. Fire through open lines rather than chasing a carry behind several blockers.|Ranged spell pressure and a repositioning tool support flexible spacing.|Missed shots and blocked lines reduce damage. Reposition around the frontline instead of abandoning all basic attacks at extreme range.

Fiddlesticks|engage|Use vision denial and terrain to hide the start of an approach. Prepare an unseen channel location before enemies arrive.|Cast Crowstorm from a location that avoids detection, then use control to keep opponents in the fight area. Tell allies which entrance you threaten.|An unseen area engage can disrupt several enemies at once.|Visible approaches lose surprise and channels can be interrupted. If the angle is exposed, reset it instead of forcing the same jump.

Fiora|duelist|Move to exposed vitals and use Riposte against the response that matters most. Prefer side-lane duels where movement is less crowded.|In a grouped fight, hit an accessible vital and protect yourself with a timed parry. Choose an ultimate target whose sides you can actually reach.|Vital damage and defensive timing reward precise one-on-one movement.|Crowded fights restrict vital access. Do not walk through multiple enemies to reach a far-side vital when peeling or side pressure is better.

Fizz|assassin|Use short trades and preserve Playful / Trickster when a critical spell is available. Approach when the target's escape is limited.|Look for an ultimate hit that allies can use, then commit after the enemy's main response. Keep a landing route out of the enemy formation.|Burst and untargetability can punish isolated or poorly protected carries.|Spending the evasive tool only for damage leaves a predictable exit. Avoid entering a group that can wait for the landing.

Galio|protect|Use wave pressure to create chances to support nearby allies. Threaten taunt when enemies must enter your space.|Choose an allied landing anchor who will still be useful when Hero's Entrance arrives. After landing, protect your damage dealers or chain control on a reachable group.|Area disruption and an allied entry point help answer enemy commitment.|An ultimate destination is tied to the ally's situation. Do not arrive at a lost position without checking who can follow.

Gangplank|control|Arrange barrels so the first safe trigger threatens the area you want. Farm while preserving barrel resources for contested space.|Set a protected barrel near your team and extend the chain toward enemies. Use Cannon Barrage to slow a route or support allies before they lose contact.|Barrel zones and long-range ultimate support can affect several parts of a fight.|Enemies can contest barrels. Avoid placing the whole damage plan where an opponent can freely remove its first link.

Garen|bruiser|Use short trades with a clear retreat, then allow passive recovery. Time Courage for the incoming retaliation.|Approach from cover or beside allies. Silence a reachable threat, spin through useful targets and use the ultimate for a realistic finish.|Simple close-range pressure, recovery and a finishing tool reward clear decisions.|Limited target access makes open-field chases costly. If a carry remains out of reach, protect your own damage source and wait for control.

Gnar|bruiser|Manage rage so the transformation matches the next contest. Use Mini form's range to build pressure without wasting the escape.|Enter a wall-side fight when Mega form is available. Choose the slam direction to put opponents into terrain while allies can follow.|Two forms combine ranged harassment with powerful area disruption.|The wrong rage timing can leave the team without an engage. Communicate the form window and delay if it is not ready.

Gragas|engage|Use barrels and body placement to threaten an approach. Preserve Body Slam when the enemy has a dangerous dive.|Choose whether Explosive Cask should separate a target, push enemies away or split their formation. Aim the displacement before throwing it.|Flexible displacement and area control can start or stop a fight.|A poorly aimed ultimate can rescue enemies or scatter them out of allied damage. Decide the intended landing area first.

Graves|marksman|Work around reloads and short attack reach. Use terrain to improve End of the Line and smoke to obstruct an enemy's view.|Attack targets that are safe to reach and use Quickdraw to maintain the angle. Put Smoke Screen on the enemy who needs vision to answer the fight.|Close-range damage and terrain interactions reward controlled skirmishes.|Bodies can block his attacks and reloads create pauses. Do not chase a backline target through a tank that absorbs the shots.

Gwen|duelist|Build Snip Snip stacks through attacks, then fight at a range where its center can connect. Use mist to control which opponents can affect you.|Place Hallowed Mist to exclude distant threats while attacking an accessible frontliner. Advance only when the next mist position remains useful.|Sustained melee damage and mist can let her fight one part of a team at a time.|Enemies who enter the mist can still fight her. Do not treat it as general invulnerability or leave it for an unnecessary chase.

Hecarim|engage|Build an approach with room to move and decide the knockback direction before contact. Use speed to improve the angle, not just to arrive first.|Approach from a side where the ultimate can disrupt the enemy formation. Push a useful target toward allies, then remain in range of their follow-up.|Fast access and area fear can force opponents to change position quickly.|An overly deep charge separates him from allied damage. Stop short of a backline dive when your team needs protection.

Heimerdinger|control|Create a turret zone before contesting ground. Fight around prepared space and use grenades to keep enemies inside it.|Set up at the entrance your team plans to hold. Choose the upgraded ability for the problem: sustained zone pressure, ranged damage or a broader control attempt.|Prepared turrets and area spells punish enemies who walk into his position.|Moving away from the setup reduces pressure. Do not follow a retreating enemy out of the zone while leaving your carry unprotected.

Hwei|control|Choose spells by purpose before pressing the sequence: damage, utility or control. Keep enough attention on positioning to avoid menu-driven tunnel vision.|Use area damage on constrained routes, select control for the approaching threat and reserve utility for safety or continued casting. Layer the ultimate onto a fight allies can sustain.|A broad spell set can answer several shapes of fight.|Using the wrong spell family costs a response window. Practise a small set of deliberate choices before attempting every combination under pressure.

Illaoi|bruiser|Build a useful tentacle area and threaten Test of Spirit. Prefer opponents coming into your space over long open-field chases.|Fight where tentacles can participate and cast the ultimate when opponents have committed near you. Keep attacking reachable targets instead of chasing those who leave.|Close clustered fights can create strong repeated area damage and recovery.|Enemies can disengage from the setup. Let them leave rather than abandoning tentacles to chase into ranged damage.

Irelia|duelist|Prepare passive stacks and use marked or finishable targets as dash routes. Plan where the route ends before taking its first step.|Enter after allied control or a useful mark. Keep track of which dashes will reset and preserve a route toward safety if the target moves away.|Fast target-to-target movement rewards prepared waves and accurate setup.|A dash without the required reset can strand her. Do not assume every low-health unit is safely finishable during a chaotic fight.

Ivern|protect|Support allies through shields, roots and brush placement. Treat Daisy as part of the team's formation rather than a pet sent away unchecked.|Shield the ally who is about to take contact, send Daisy to disrupt a useful target and root threats your team can act on. Keep your own body out of the dive.|Protection and an extra disruptive unit support extended allied fights.|Brush changes vision for both teams and a root can tempt unsafe movement. Check the destination before following or encouraging a forward dash.

Janna|protect|Keep the tools that stop an approach ready when enemy engage is available. Use movement to stay close enough to protect without becoming the first target.|Interrupt the incoming threat with tornado or displacement. Use Monsoon when its knockback and healing protect the fight, rather than pushing enemies out of an ally's winning combo.|Strong disengage can undo an enemy's committed entry.|Spending control for minor poke creates an opening. Save at least one answer for the enemy who can reach your carry.

JarvanIV|engage|Use the flag-and-drag line to threaten entry and terrain crossing. Decide whether your team wants a trapped target before committing.|Engage on an opponent allies can reach, then use Cataclysm to restrict a useful area. Remove the terrain if it traps allies in danger or blocks their pursuit.|Long entry and temporary terrain can isolate targets or split formations.|The arena can harm friendly movement. Watch allied positions after casting instead of treating the terrain as always beneficial.

Jax|duelist|Build pressure through repeated attacks and time Counter Strike for the opponent's attack window. Save Leap Strike for meaningful access or escape.|Hit the nearest useful target while preparing the stun. Jump deeper only when enemy control is spent and your allies can support the landing.|Sustained attack pressure and a defensive stun window support duels and cleanup.|Blindly jumping onto a carry invites layered control. If the access is poor, use the stun to stop the enemy frontline.

Jayce|poke|Use ranged pressure to weaken opponents before changing forms. Choose melee form when close contact is deliberate, not automatic.|Fire through an acceleration gate from protected ground. Keep hammer knockback available for a diver and switch into melee only for a safe follow-up.|Two forms provide ranged pressure and a close-range response.|A missed poke sequence or early melee entry loses the distance advantage. Reset your firing angle instead of forcing a dive.

Jhin|marksman|Plan movement around the four-shot cycle and place traps on approaches. Use allied damage to set up a long-range root.|Fire from a protected edge and use Deadly Flourish on a marked target allies can reach. Start Curtain Call from a position enemies cannot immediately invade.|Long-range follow-up and powerful timed shots reward coordinated catches.|Reloads and an immobile ultimate channel create windows of weakness. Do not channel while a missing diver can reach your position.

Jinx|marksman|Choose rockets for useful range and area pressure, then use the minigun when sustained close contact is safe. Save traps for a route that matters.|Damage a safe target until a takedown creates a reset opportunity. Move forward with the speed only after checking the next enemy threat.|A first takedown can turn steady damage into rapid cleanup.|Before a reset, she is vulnerable to access. Do not run past protection merely because a low-health target could trigger the passive.

Kaisa|marksman|Combine attacks and spells to finish Plasma on reachable targets. Use movement and evolution tools to maintain safe contact.|Start by damaging the frontline if needed. Use Killer Instinct to reposition toward a marked target only when the destination is survivable and allies can support it.|Follow-up access and burst on marked targets allow fast changes of angle.|The ultimate can place her beside the whole enemy team. Choose the landing side carefully and do not use every mark as an invitation.

Kalista|marksman|Move between attacks and build spears on targets you can keep hitting. Coordinate the oathsworn ally's role before fighting.|Keep a clear hop route while stacking Rend. Use Fate's Call to save or launch your partner according to the fight, with a shared target in mind.|Repeated movement and a coordinated partner can sustain pressure and create control.|Crowded terrain and movement disruption reduce her spacing options. Avoid hopping toward a wall or into the enemy approach.

Karma|protect|Use Mantra for the current need rather than a fixed damage routine. Poke when safe, but keep resources for the ally who must move.|Shield and speed the team through a dangerous approach or retreat. Tether an accessible threat when you can stay in range without being isolated.|Flexible shielding, speed and ranged pressure help the team change position.|A tether requires continued proximity. Do not chase its completion into a place where your shield cannot keep you alive.

Karthus|control|Place Lay Waste where the opponent will move and use the wall to constrain their route. Manage mana before a long contest.|Damage the reachable fight area from behind protection. If killed, use the passive window deliberately; choose an ultimate channel that will not waste the active fight opportunity.|Persistent area damage and a map-wide ultimate can contribute across distance.|Dying early removes positioning choice even if spells remain available briefly. Do not treat the passive as a reason to give away a preventable death.

Kassadin|assassin|Use safe farming and short spell exchanges to reach stronger mobility windows. Track the cost of repeated Riftwalk casts.|Wait for enemy control to be spent, then enter from an edge and leave before the next response. Keep enough mana for the return jump.|Repeated teleport movement supports late-fight target access and cleanup.|Repeated ultimate use consumes resources quickly. A reachable target is not safe if the next cast needed to escape is unaffordable.

Katarina|assassin|Place daggers to create movement and damage choices. Wait for a usable reset opportunity instead of entering solely because Shunpo is ready.|Track the enemy spell that can interrupt Death Lotus. Follow allied damage onto a vulnerable target, then reassess each reset before jumping again.|Takedown resets can let her change targets rapidly in a damaged team.|Predictable dagger locations and available control punish early entry. Do not channel in front of a ready interrupt.

Kayle|marksman|Protect early development and adapt to the reach available at the current level. Choose farm and safe trades over unnecessary early commitments.|Deal sustained damage from a protected position. Use Divine Judgment on the ally whose survival will decide the next seconds, including yourself when you are the target.|Scaling attacks and a strong defensive ultimate support prolonged fights.|The ultimate has a limited window. Avoid using it for harmless poke, then entering the real fight without protection.

Kayn|bruiser|Choose the form's job: Shadow Assassin seeks vulnerable targets; Rhaast prefers sustained melee contact. Use terrain travel to select an approach.|In assassin form, enter after protection is spent and leave quickly. As Rhaast, fight reachable durable targets and use the ultimate to bridge a dangerous damage window.|Form choice creates either flank burst or sustained frontline pressure.|A plan for one form does not automatically fit the other. Do not play Rhaast as a single-pass assassin or remain trading as Shadow Assassin.

Kennen|engage|Apply marks through safe ranged pressure and preserve an approach for the ultimate. Threaten a flank before enemies settle into position.|Enter from an unseen or protected angle with Slicing Maelstrom ready. Stay near multiple useful targets while allies follow the stun window.|Area damage and repeated marks can disrupt a compact enemy team.|A visible direct approach invites disengage. Wait for allied setup or improve the flank rather than running through every enemy spell.

Khazix|assassin|Seek isolated targets and use terrain to approach without crossing the frontline. Reassess isolation as allies move near the target.|Wait at the edge until a vulnerable enemy separates. Use invisibility to change timing and keep Leap for access or escape according to the situation.|Isolation pressure makes separated enemies costly to leave unprotected.|Grouped opponents reduce favorable targets. Do not jump into a cluster expecting the same damage pattern as a lone target.

Kindred|marksman|Use ranged attacks and short dashes to maintain contact. Treat marks as opportunities that still require vision and team support.|Hold Lamb's Respite for a meaningful lethal window and plan what happens when it ends. Position so allies can use the zone without giving enemies a free escape.|Ranged sustained damage and a death-prevention zone can reverse a burst attempt.|The zone protects enemies too. Track who benefits at expiry rather than casting merely because anyone is low.

Kled|bruiser|Fight around mounted and dismounted states and make remount opportunities deliberate. Use tether pressure to discourage easy retreat.|Lead a charge along a route allies can follow. After contact, focus an accessible target and reassess your risk when Skaarl leaves.|Aggressive entry and remount threat reward sustained close combat.|Dismounting changes mobility and safety. Do not assume a remount will happen before the enemy finishes its next damage sequence.

KogMaw|marksman|Use the attack-range window to damage safe targets and move during its downtime. Keep allies between you and immediate threats.|Activate Bio-Arcane Barrage when targets are actually reachable. Attack the frontline from protection and use artillery to pressure enemies leaving your attack range.|Extended ranged attacks can threaten durable targets in a protected formation.|No dash makes flank access dangerous. Do not sacrifice position to keep one more attack going after protection moves away.

KSante|protect|Use defensive tools and control to hold the frontline. Treat All Out as a change in responsibility, not a required opener.|Start by disrupting threats to your carry. Isolate an enemy with the ultimate only if leaving the main formation will improve the fight.|Flexible displacement and a defensive stance can control close engagements.|All Out trades safety for aggression. Do not abandon an exposed carry or take a duel you cannot finish.

Leblanc|assassin|Use brief spell sequences and return points to create threat without remaining in range. Approach from vision gaps when possible.|Pressure an exposed carry from the side, then return before the enemy locks down the landing point. Use chains on a diver when backline access is poor.|Burst and return movement enable repeated threats from changing angles.|Enemies can watch the return pad. Keep track of both positions instead of assuming the return is always safe.

LeeSin|bruiser|Use spell and attack sequencing to keep energy available. Plan a ward or allied unit route before moving into danger.|Choose a useful Dragon's Rage direction: kick a threat away or deliver a target toward allies. Follow Sonic Wave only after checking the landing point.|Mobility and displacement offer many ways to change a small fight.|A hit Q does not require a second cast. Avoid following into a group just to attempt a difficult kick.

Leona|engage|Threaten contact while staying within allied follow-up range. Layer control so its duration is useful instead of overlapping every effect.|Use the ultimate to start a reachable catch or stop a diver. Follow with Zenith Blade only when your team can arrive before the target recovers.|Several control tools make a clear target easy for allies to attack.|She has limited retreat once committed. If the team is backing away, protect the retreat rather than selecting a new engage.

Lillia|bruiser|Keep movement available through repeated spell hits and use the outer swing to pressure. Work around the edge of melee range.|Apply Dream Dust to useful targets before the ultimate. Signal the sleep window so allies can prepare damage instead of taking an uncoordinated early hit.|Movement and multi-target sleep can turn scattered contact into a coordinated fight.|She must expose herself to apply effects. Do not run through the whole team solely to add one more sleep target.

Lissandra|engage|Use wave pressure and terrain-assisted claw paths to threaten close-range control. Keep a clear choice between self-cast and enemy-cast ultimate.|Enter after confirming allied follow-up, root the nearby threats and choose the ultimate target by survival and control needs. Self-cast can buy time inside a committed fight.|Reliable close control and defensive stasis support decisive entries.|A deep claw recast can strand her. A good self-ultimate delays damage but does not guarantee allies can reach her afterward.

Locke|bruiser|Land Ritual Nails and follow with attacks to use the marks. Treat Soul Ignition's self-damage as a resource cost, even with delayed recovery.|Use Ashen Pursuit from an angle your team can support.
